questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Curvature of a Plane Curve
questions.problem: Using the cross product curvature formula, find the curvature of $r(t)=⟨{sin}^{2}⁡t-{cos}^{2}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩$ at the point where $t=\frac{\pi }{4}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The curvature $κ(t)$ is given by

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}.
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$, ${r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}),$ and $‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({sin}^{2}⁡t-{cos}^{2}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\  & =⟨2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =⟨2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{4}),\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{\pi }{4}⟩=⟨2,\sqrt{2}⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖ & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(\sqrt{2})^{2}}=\sqrt{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find ${r}^{″}(t)$ and ${r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨4\operatorname{cos}⁡2t,\,-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =⟨4\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{4}),\,-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{\pi }{4}⟩=⟨0,\,-\sqrt{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the cross product by considering ${r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})$ and ${r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4})$ as $3$-dimensional vectors with zero $z$-components:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})\times {r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =⟨2,\,\sqrt{2},0⟩\times ⟨0,\,-\sqrt{2},\,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & \sqrt{2} & 0 \\ 0 & -\sqrt{2} & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}2 & \sqrt{2} \\ 0 & -\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =-2\sqrt{2}\,k \\ ‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})\times {r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖ & =2\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the curvature at $t=\frac{\pi }{4}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})\times {r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖}{{‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖}^{3}}=\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{(\sqrt{6})^{3}}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Given the curve $r(t)=⟨{t}^{2}+1,\,{t}^{2}-1,\,2t⟩$, use the cross product curvature formula to find the curvature as a function of $t.$
questions.worked_solution:
The curvature $κ(t)$ is given by

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}.
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}+1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)⟩=⟨2t,\,2t,\,2⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(2t)^{2}+(2t)^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+4{t}^{2}+4} \\  & =\sqrt{4(2{t}^{2}+1)} \\  & =2\sqrt{2{t}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the second derivative ${r}^{″}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2)⟩=⟨2,\,2,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the cross-product:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t) & =⟨2t,2t,2⟩\times ⟨2,2,0⟩ \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2t & 2t & 2 \\ 2 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2t & 2 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}2t & 2 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}2t & 2t \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}|k \\  & =-4i+4j+(4t-4t)k \\  & =-4\,i+4\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute the magnitude of the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(-4)^{2}+{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{32} \\  & =4\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}=\frac{4\sqrt{2}}{{[2\sqrt{2{t}^{2}+1}]}^{3}}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2(2{t}^{2}+1)^{3/2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given the curve $r(t)=⟨3\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,4t⟩,$ use the cross product curvature formula to find the curvature of this curve as a function of $t.$ 

*Hint: You can use the fact that ${r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)=12\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i-12\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j-9k.$*
questions.worked_solution:
The curvature $κ(t)$ is given by

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}.
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t)⟩ \\  & =⟨3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,4⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}+{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9{cos}^{2}⁡t+9{sin}^{2}⁡t+16} \\  & =\sqrt{25} \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Since we are told that

$$
{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)=12\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i-12\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j-9k,
$$

we have

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(12\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{(-12\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}+{(-9)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{144+81} \\  & =15\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{15}{{5}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{3}{25}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Curvature of a Plane Curve
questions.problem: Using the cross product curvature formula, find the curvature of $r(t)=⟨{e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,{e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩$ as a function of $t.$
questions.worked_solution:
The curvature $κ$ is given by

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}.
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-{e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t-{e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,{e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t-{e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\  & ={e}^{-t}⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & ={e}^{-t}\sqrt{{(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}+{(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}} \\  & ={e}^{-t}\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡t+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t} \\  & ={e}^{-t}\sqrt{2({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\sqrt{2}{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the second derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t-{e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t-{e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2{e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-2{e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\  & =2{e}^{-t}⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the cross product by considering ${r}^{′}(t)$ and ${r}^{″}(t)$ as $3$-dimensional vectors with zero $z$-components:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t) & =({e}^{-t}⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0⟩)\times (2{e}^{-t}⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,0⟩) \\  & =2{e}^{-2t}\,\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t & \operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t & 0 \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡t & -\operatorname{cos}⁡t & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =2{e}^{-2t}\,\left|\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t & \operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡t & -\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =2{e}^{-2t}({cos}^{2}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)k \\  & =2{e}^{-2t}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

So, the magnitude of the cross product is

$$
‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖=2{e}^{-2t}.
$$

Therefore, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{2{e}^{-2t}}{{(\sqrt{2}{e}^{-t})}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{2{e}^{-2t}}{2\sqrt{2}{e}^{-3t}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}{e}^{t}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Curvature of a Curve at a General Point
questions.problem:
Given the curve $r(t)=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡2t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡2t,\,2t⟩,$  use the cross product curvature formula to find the curvature of this curve as a function of $t.$ 

*Hint: You can use the fact that ${r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)=8(\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,i-\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,j+\,k).$*
questions.worked_solution:
The curvature $κ(t)$ is given by

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}.
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t,\,2⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)}^{2}+{(2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)}^{2}+{(2)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{sin}^{2}⁡2t+4{cos}^{2}⁡2t+4} \\  & =\sqrt{4({sin}^{2}⁡2t+{cos}^{2}⁡2t)+4} \\  & =\sqrt{4+4} \\  & =2\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Since we are told that

$$
{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)=8(\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,i-\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,j+\,k),
$$

we have

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖ & =8\sqrt{(\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)^{2}+(-\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)^{2}+(1)^{2}} \\  & =8\sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡2t+{cos}^{2}⁡2t+1} \\  & =8\sqrt{1+1} \\  & =8\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{8\sqrt{2}}{{(2\sqrt{2})}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{8\sqrt{2}}{16\sqrt{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
